import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Income distribution by education level
income_edu_data = df[df['Income'] < 200000]  # Filter outliers for better visualization
sns.boxplot(data=income_edu_data, x='Education', y='Income', ax=axes[0, 0], palette='viridis')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Annual Income ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Spending patterns across product categories
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 
                 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_data = df[spending_cols].sum().reset_index()
spending_data.columns = ['Product Category', 'Total Spending']
spending_data['Product Category'] = spending_data['Product Category'].str.replace('Mnt', '').str.replace('Prods', 'Products')

colors = plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(spending_data)))
bars = axes[0, 1].bar(spending_data['Product Category'], spending_data['Total Spending'], color=colors)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Total Spending Across Product Categories', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Product Category', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Total Spending Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[0, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 50000,
                   f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 3. Purchase channels distribution
purchase_channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_data = df[purchase_channels].sum().reset_index()
purchase_data.columns = ['Channel', 'Total Purchases']
purchase_data['Channel'] = purchase_data['Channel'].str.replace('Num', '').str.replace('Purchases', '')

wedges, texts, autotexts = axes[1, 0].pie(purchase_data['Total Purchases'], labels=purchase_data['Channel'], 
                                          autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=['#ff9999','#66b3ff','#99ff99'])
axes[1, 0].set_title('Distribution of Purchases by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Customer demographics: Marital status distribution
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
bars2 = axes[1, 1].bar(marital_counts.index, marital_counts.values, color=plt.cm.Paired(np.arange(len(marital_counts))))
axes[1, 1].set_title('Customer Distribution by Marital Status', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Marital Status', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars2:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 20,
                   f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# Adjust layout and add overall title
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis: Demographics, Spending Patterns, and Purchase Behavior', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
